title: Unified catalog adapter + profile publish pipeline for embeddings->reranker onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Teams that deploy embedding models followed by reranker models need a repeatable, low-friction onboarding flow that guarantees reproducible performance profiles and safe version pinning. Today we have two separate ingestion paths: embeddings onboarding and reranker onboarding. That fragmentation causes duplicated steps, stale profile entries, and occasional mismatches when customers pin an embedding version that is incompatible with the reranker profile.

Goal: Build a unified catalog adapter that normalizes model metadata (architecture, tokenizer, quantization, hardware hints) from both embedding and reranker onboarding sheets and a profile publish pipeline that atomically registers performance profiles and associated pinning metadata. The pipeline should: validate incoming profiles, dedupe near-duplicate profiles, sign artifacts for provenance, and expose a pinning surface for Console and the API so customers can pin a consistent pair or contract (embedding+reranker).

Out of scope: UI redesign for Console (we will expose a minimal pinning endpoint and Console PM will iterate separately), training dataset ingestion (only metadata), automated retraining or model conversion steps.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog adapter accepts embeddings and reranker manifests and writes normalized metadata to model-catalog with consistent field names
Profile publish pipeline validates metric schema (latency, throughput, recall@k, MRR) and rejects profiles missing required keys
Profiles that are <=1% different on core metrics are deduplicated and merged with provenance preserved
Published profiles are signed and stored with an immutable artifact URL and checksum
A new API endpoint exists to create a pin contract that references an embedding model id and reranker model id (or variants) and returns a pin id
Console and SDK show the pin id and associated profile summary (for later rollout decisions)
Integration tests exercise end-to-end onboarding: manifest -> catalog -> profile publish -> pin creation
Monitoring dashboard tracks publish success/failure rate, validation errors, and time-to-publish (SLO: 95% < 60s)
Backward compatibility: existing embedding-only and reranker-only onboarding flows continue to work
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design adapter schema (fields: model_family, arch, tokenizer_hash, quantization_profile, avg_seq_len, example_types, eval_harness_id)
Phase 1: Add manifest parser module and unit tests; provide CLI for manual ingestion (dev-only)
Phase 2: Profile validation service: implement schema checks, required metric enforcement, and basic statistical fingerprinting
Phase 2: Dedup/merge service that computes similarity of numeric metrics and textual tags; produce merged profile with provenance array
Phase 3: Artifact signing: wire KMS signing for profile metadata and store signed payload in artifact storage with checksum
Phase 3: Pinning API and database schema: pins table supports multiple model roles (embedding, reranker) and a human-friendly pin label
Phase 4: Integrations: connect publish pipeline to eval harness to populate eval_harness_id and link to open PRs or datasets
Phase 4: Add monitoring, alerting, and a dashboard card in Console for published profiles
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use a single normalized catalog schema to reduce cross-team friction, even though it will require a migration step for older catalog entries
Perform dedupe at publish time (strong consistency) rather than background job to give immediate feedback to publishers; tradeoff: higher tail latency during publish
Sign artifacts with KMS to ensure provenance at the cost of an extra KMS call per publish; mitigated with a signing queue and batched signing for high-throughput jobs
Store merged profile as a new immutable artifact rather than overwriting to preserve historical regressions for rollbacks
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser with 10+ real-world manifests (open-source and internal)
Integration test: run full pipeline against a synthetic eval harness that emits known metrics and assert published checksum and pin creation
Load test: simulate 100 concurrent publishes to validate publish SLO and dedupe behaviour
Canary: enable new publish pipeline for internal teams and 5 customers; collect feedback for 2 weeks before full rollout
